content.value_statement: Prisma MongoDB projects cannot upgrade to Prisma ORM v7 because it has no MongoDB connector. This skill helps teams assess blockers, remain secure on v6, or plan a staged Prisma Next evaluation.
actual_capabilities: Explains why Prisma ORM v7 is not an upgrade target for MongoDB projects.
Identifies transaction support and pre-1.0 change tolerance as migration decision factors.
Maps v6 MongoDB schema concepts to Prisma Next contract concepts.
Describes the Prisma Next plan, migrate, verify, and sign lifecycle.
Provides a staged cutover approach using the same database and index checks.
limitations: Does not execute migrations, alter schemas, or change database data.
Does not replace Prisma Next documentation for the installed version.
Does not guarantee feature parity for every Prisma Client API or transaction workflow.
Requires users to verify Prisma Next behavior and MongoDB compatibility before production changes.

use_cases.title: Evaluate an upgrade path
use_cases.description: Determine whether a MongoDB application should stay on Prisma ORM v6 or assess Prisma Next.

use_cases.title: Prepare a migration plan
use_cases.description: Map schema, client API, and migration workflow changes before testing a Prisma Next transition.

use_cases.title: Review cutover readiness
use_cases.description: Use the staged checklist to validate server version, indexes, contracts, and rollback planning.

prompt_templates.title: Check upgrade options
prompt_templates.prompt: Our Prisma project uses MongoDB. Explain whether we can upgrade to Prisma ORM v7 and what options we have.

prompt_templates.title: Assess migration blockers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our Prisma MongoDB project for Prisma Next migration blockers, especially transaction usage and supported MongoDB versions.

prompt_templates.title: Map schema changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Help map our Prisma ORM v6 MongoDB schema concepts to Prisma Next contracts. List items we must verify against our installed version.

prompt_templates.title: Create a staged cutover plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cautious Prisma Next migration plan for our MongoDB service. Include contract review, migration verification, index parity, approval gates, and rollback preparation.

output_examples.input: Can we upgrade our Prisma MongoDB application to Prisma ORM v7?
output: Prisma ORM v7 does not include a MongoDB connector.
Keep Prisma ORM v6 for a stable path, or evaluate Prisma Next with a staged test.
Verify installed Prisma Next capabilities before planning production changes.

output_examples.input: What should we verify before moving a MongoDB service to Prisma Next?
output: Confirm MongoDB server compatibility and the required MongoDB driver version.
Identify multi-document transaction usage and plan raw-driver alternatives if needed.
Test contract, migration, verification, indexes, and application behavior on a staged copy.

best_practices: Verify Prisma Next behavior against the versions installed in the project.
Review migration plans and obtain explicit approval before applying database changes.
Test cutover steps on a staged copy before changing production systems.
anti_patterns: Do not recommend Prisma ORM v7 as a MongoDB upgrade path.
Do not replace MongoDB with SQL as an implicit response to an ORM upgrade request.
Do not apply push-style production changes without migration history and verification.

faq.question: Can a Prisma MongoDB project upgrade to Prisma ORM v7?
faq.answer: No. Prisma ORM v7 has no MongoDB connector.

faq.question: What is the stable option for MongoDB projects?
faq.answer: Remain on the latest Prisma ORM v6 patch release while monitoring updates and advisories.

faq.question: What is Prisma Next?
faq.answer: Prisma Next is the successor path described by this skill. Its MongoDB support is Early Access.

faq.question: Does this skill run database migrations?
faq.answer: No. It provides decision and planning guidance only.

faq.question: What should teams check before trying Prisma Next?
faq.answer: Check MongoDB server compatibility, installed package versions, transaction use, and feature parity.

faq.question: How should production changes be handled?
faq.answer: Review the migration plan, test it in a staged environment, and explicitly approve production execution.
